start.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocode of the place name "10th of Ramadan City, Sharqia, Egypt" (OSM way 605783816, place=city centroid) — a CITY-level centroid, not a station-level pinpoint. No Overpass query for man_made=pipeline or a named PRM/pressure-reduction facility in the 10th of Ramadan area returned any mapped feature, so no more precise coordinate could be obtained from OSM.

end.name: unresolved — no named origin/tie-in point found

corridor_note: P8079 is a short (4.5 km) GASCO spur feeding the 10th of Ramadan industrial city's gas network. GASCO's own live gas-grid page (gasco.com.eg/index.php/gas-grid/) confirms the 10th of Ramadan concession is fed by GASCO distribution lines of "2 in to 16 in" diameter, matching GEM's 16 in spec, and the almalnews.com 2024 article ("جاسكو تنفذ 5 خطوط جديدة لتدعيم الشبكة القومية للغازات") independently lists "خط غاز العاشر من رمضان" (10th of Ramadan gas line) among GASCO's completed national-grid reinforcement projects and separately names "العاشر من رمضان" as one of GASCO's four named pressure-reduction & measurement (P.R.M. / تخفيض وقياس) stations — so the pipeline's IDENTITY and terminus city are well corroborated by two independent live sources. What could not be found in any public source (Arabic or English; GASCO's own site, Ministry of Petroleum reporting, egy-map.com/presidency.eg project database, OSM/Overpass) is a named origin point — i.e. which upstream trunk or compressor/metering station this spur taps into before reaching the 10th of Ramadan city-gate/PRM station. GASCO does not publish a line-by-line from/to table for its internal distribution spurs the way the presidency.eg project database does for larger feed lines, and OSM has zero mapped pipeline infrastructure in the bounding box around 10th of Ramadan City. Given the very short 4.5 km length and Al-Sharqia-governorate-both-ends attribute, the most plausible reading is a short tie-in from a nearby trunk (e.g. a branch of the national grid running through Sharqia) directly to the city's PRM station, but this is inference, not a sourced fact, and is NOT presented as a finding.
length_check: Cannot be computed — only one endpoint (approximate, city-centroid precision) was obtained, so no meaningful endpoint-separation distance exists to compare against GEM's stated 4.5 km. Given the short length, a city-centroid-to-unknown-origin haversine would not be a meaningful sanity check even if attempted.
notes: Identity of the pipeline (a real, named GASCO PRM feed line to 10th of Ramadan City) is corroborated by two independent live sources (GASCO's own site + almalnews.com), so this is not a case of an unverifiable or dubious pipeline — it is a real, well-attested facility whose PRECISE geometry/second endpoint simply is not published anywhere found. Do not force a guessed origin point into the geometry ladder; escalate to the corridor-partial bucket. The almalnews.com article is also the sole source independently corroborating BOTH P8079 and P8080 together (it lists both the 10th of Ramadan line and the West Cairo/Waleidia power-plant feed lines in the same GASCO project roundup), which is useful cross-context for a reviewer but does not itself supply coordinates for either.

end.name: Cairo West Power Plant (محطة كهرباء غرب القاهرة), operated by Cairo Electricity Production Company
end.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Overpass query for power=plant tagged "Cairo West Power Plant" (way 807008190), center point as returned by Overpass `out center;`. The plant's own operator site (cairoepc.com) independently confirms the plant name/identity and states it is physically located at "سقيل – الجيزة" (Giza), which was cross-checked by reverse-geocoding the OSM coordinate via Nominatim: result address.state = "الجيزة" (Giza), ISO3166-2-lvl4 = EG-GZ.

corridor_note: "P.S." in the GEM pipeline name "West Cairo P.S. Gas Pipeline" = Power Station, not pressure station — confirmed by an exact, government-sourced project match. The public Egyptian presidential project-tracking database (mirrored live at egy-map.com, which explicitly attributes its content to "نقلا من الموقع الرسمي لرئاسة الجمهورية" / reproduced from the official Presidency website, since presidency.eg itself blocks scraper access with a 403 WAF) lists a project titled "إنشاء خط تغذية محطة كهرباء غرب القاهرة" (Construction of a feed line for the West Cairo power station), filed under Cairo governorate, completed June 2020, cost 403 million EGP, describing the project explicitly as "إنشاء خط بطول 16 كم وقطر 30 بوصة لتغذية محطة كهرباء غرب القاهرة بالغاز" (a 16 km line of 30-inch diameter to feed West Cairo power station with gas) — an EXACT match to GEM's 16.0 km / 30 in spec, date, and pipeline purpose. This independently confirms the pipeline's identity, length, diameter, destination, and governorate filing beyond reasonable doubt. It is independently corroborated by almalnews.com's 2024 GASCO article, which separately lists "تغذية محطتى كهرباء الوليدية وغرب القاهرة" (feeding the Waleidia and West Cairo power plants) among GASCO's completed prior-year national-grid projects. However: the DESTINATION plant itself (Cairo West / "West Cairo" power plant) sits physically in Giza governorate per BOTH OSM's independent tagging and the plant operator's own site (cairoepc.com: "تقع المحطة سقيل – الجيزة"), not Cairo governorate — a genuine, sourced discrepancy between GEM's "Cairo governorate both ends" attribute (which mirrors the government pipeline-project database's own Cairo filing) and the terminus facility's actual governorate. The most plausible non-speculative reading is that the pipeline's route corridor runs mostly or entirely through Cairo governorate territory even though its physical terminus (the plant) sits at or just past the Cairo/Giza boundary — but this is presented as a documented open question, not a resolved fact. No source found (Arabic or English) names the pipeline's ORIGIN / tie-in point on the national grid; the government project record describes only the destination and specs, not a from/to pair.
length_check: Cannot be computed as a full endpoint-separation distance — only the destination (Cairo West Power Plant) endpoint is pinned; the origin is unresolved. The 16.0 km / 30 in length and diameter are independently confirmed at the project level (not geometrically re-derived) by the egy-map.com/presidency.eg project record, which states the built line length as exactly 16 km, matching GEM's sheet value precisely.
notes: This pipeline's IDENTITY, length, diameter, cost, completion date and destination are unusually well sourced (an exact government-project-database match) — the open gap is purely geometric (no origin point named anywhere public) and a minor governorate nuance at the destination end, not a doubt about whether the pipeline exists or what it is. A reviewer drawing this corridor should treat the Cairo West Power Plant point as a solid, high-confidence terminus and should not force an origin guess; flag as a corridor partial pending a named origin (most likely a nearby national-grid trunk or city-gate station west of Cairo, but unconfirmed).

start.name: Abu Sultan Power Station (محطة كهرباء أبو سلطان البخارية), operated by East Delta Electricity Production Company
start.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Overpass query for power=plant tagged "Abu Sultan Power Station" (way 105569177), center point as returned by Overpass `out center;`. Independently cross-checked via a separate OSM Nominatim search for "Abu Sultan, Ismailia, Egypt" which returned a landuse=industrial node "محطة كهرباء أبو سلطان البخارية" at lat 30.4022965, lon 32.3079728 — within ~30 m of the Overpass power=plant centroid, i.e. two independently-queried OSM features agreeing on the same location. Reverse-geocoding this point confirms it lies in Al-Ismailia governorate (ISO3166-2-lvl4 EG-IS), matching GEM's "Ismailia governorate" attribute.

end.name: Shabab Power Station (محطة كهرباء الشباب), operated by East Delta Electricity Production Company
end.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Overpass query for power=plant tagged "Shabab Power Station" (way 124777337), center point as returned by Overpass `out center;`. Reverse-geocoding this point confirms it lies in Al-Ismailia governorate (ISO3166-2-lvl4 EG-IS), matching GEM's "Ismailia governorate" attribute for both ends.

corridor_note: Not applicable — both endpoints are resolved. "El Shabab" in the GEM pipeline name refers to the Shabab (الشباب) power station near Tell El Kebir, Ismailia governorate, operated by East Delta Electricity Production Company (1,500 MW combined-cycle, gas-fired) — the same "الشباب" also named independently in almalnews.com's 2024 GASCO article as one of GASCO's four named pressure-reduction & measurement (P.R.M.) stations undergoing renewal ("الشباب الجديدة"), confirming "Shabab" is a real, recurring, named facility in GASCO/EEHC infrastructure terminology rather than a generic or ambiguous term. The pipeline connects this station to the Abu Sultan power station (600 MW, gas-fired, in service since 1983) near Lake Timsah/Great Bitter Lake, Ismailia governorate — both facilities are EEHC/East Delta Electricity Production Company assets reported in the same government annual report (moee.gov.eg EEHC_Rep 2017-2018), and both are documented with separate Wikidata entries. A contractor project-history search (civecon.com, a Petrojet-affiliated EPC contractor site) was seen earlier in this research session explicitly describing an "Abu Sultan – Shabab Power Plant" gas pipeline project, which would be a strong third independent corroboration of this exact pipeline's identity — but the specific project-page URL could not be re-located or re-verified before filing this deliverable (a later attempt found only civecon.com's homepage, which does not itself name the project), so per the no-fabricated-URL rule it is NOT included in refs/urls_verified. The finding rests instead on the two power-plant identities (OSM + government report + Wikidata) plus the quantitative length match below.
length_check: Haversine great-circle distance between the two resolved endpoints (30.4025419,32.3077692) and (30.4655438,31.9247594) = 37.38 km, versus GEM's stated pipeline length of 38.0 km — a 98.4% match (0.62 km / 1.6% short, consistent with a great-circle lower bound against a real pipeline corridor that is not perfectly straight). This is strong quantitative corroboration that these are the correct two endpoints.
notes: Highest-confidence result of the three PIDs in this batch. Both endpoints are named, government-report-sourced facilities, independently geocoded via OSM, both confirmed to sit in Ismailia governorate per Nominatim reverse geocoding (matching GEM's attribute), and the great-circle separation closely matches the sheet length. Suitable for the endpoints rung of the §8 geometry ladder as-is; a human corridor pass should still draw the actual pipe route (it will follow roads/canals around Lake Timsah / the Ismailia canal corridor rather than a straight line) rather than using the great-circle segment directly.
